lines.li: [them] The elders tell of {HOUSE} at our fire, and the children ask for it again.
[us] I hope they tell it kindly.
[them] Kindly enough, and a little longer each time.
[them] There's a song about {HOUSE} in our hall now, if you can believe it.
[us] Is it a good one?
[them] The tune's good, and most of the words are true.
[them] Your family's in the papers back home, {HOUSE} by name.
[us] Page one, I hope.
[them] Page two, but it's a good page.
[them] Your family's name comes up on our channels, {HOUSE}.
[us] In a good way, I hope.
[them] In a way that makes people stop and listen.
[them] At court one hears {HOUSE} spoken of now and then.
[us] What do they say?
[them] That your family is worth knowing, which at court is high praise.
[them] Even people who've never seen your colony know {HOUSE}.
[us] That's strange to hear.
[them] Your family's name is {RENOWN}, so get used to it.
[them] A family whose name is {RENOWN} would make a fine match for one of ours.
[us] Maybe, if the one of yours is willing.
[them] We'll see who's willing, then.
[them] My town would welcome one of {HOUSE} at its table any day.
[us] That's kind of you.
[them] It's sense, a name like yours is worth having near.
[them] I've heard of {HOUSE} back home, though not much yet.
[us] What did you hear?
[them] That your family is {RENOWN}, more or less.
[them] Which family are you of, here?
[us] I'm of {HOUSE}.
[them] I don't know the name yet.
[us] Give it time.
[them] Among us a family earns its name by what it does for the clan.
[us] Then ours is still earning.
[them] Good, the earning is the best part.
[them] Your family's known for {KNOWNFOR} where I come from.
[us] We've had to be.
[them,their:tribal] Our young hunters want to wrestle one of you to see.
[them] Some of our young ones want to try their luck against one of you.
[them] Our captain says your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and he doesn't praise easily.
[us] Tell him thank you.
[them] He'd say there's nothing to thank him for.
[them] A family known for {KNOWNFOR} might find a place in the Empire's ranks.
[us] We're needed here.
[them] A pity, the Empire rewards its soldiers well.
[them] I heard about the raid, your family's {KNOWNFOR} must have been needed.
[us] They were.
[them] Then I'm glad they were here.
[them] They say your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and people remember who healed them.
[us] We do what we can for anyone hurt.
[them] That's why they remember.
[them] With sickness at home, people there talk about your family's {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] If anyone needs looking at, bring them by.
[them] I'll tell them you said so.
[them] Our healer has heard that your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Maybe the two of them could trade what they know.
[them] Our healer would like that, if the elders allow it.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and I can see why.
[us] Sit down, then, there's room.
[them,their:lowtech] I'll sit, and gladly.
[them] Don't mind if I do.
[them] Your family's known for {KNOWNFOR}, I'm told.
[us] Fair, I hope you were told.
[them] Fair, and hard to get the better of.
[them] Your family's known for {KNOWNFOR}, it's in our trade notes.
[us] Is that good or bad for us?
[them] Good for you, bad for our margins.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and I'd like to see some of it.
[us] Look around, a fair bit of what's here is ours.
[them] I'm looking.
[them] Your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}, even among us.
[us,samefaith] Then we pray to the same, and that's good company.
[us] We keep to what we believe, that's all.
[them] That's more than most manage.
[them] People of faith we meet on the road ask about your family.
[us] They'd be welcome here.
[them] I'll tell them so.
[them] Your family's name isn't a good one where I come from.
[us] People say a lot of things.
[them] They say this one often.
[them] I'd rather not be seen talking with one of {HOUSE}.
[us] Then walk on.
[them] Your family has a name for trouble, but you seem all right.
[us] Most of us are.
[them] Then maybe the name will change.
[us] You're the head of {THEIRHOUSE}, aren't you?
[them] I am, for my sins.
[us] It must keep you busy.
[them] Busier than the town does, some days.
[us] Even here we hear about {THEIRHOUSE}.
[them] Good things, I hope.
[us] Mostly good things.
[us] Your family's totem, what is it?
[them] That is told only to those who have earned it.
[us] Then I'll keep earning.
[us] What's on your family's arms, if you don't mind me asking?
[them] A tower and a plow, the oldest of us chose it.
[us] Plain, but it says something.
[them] The fighting with {THEN} still goes on, you know.
[us] I'd hoped it was over.
[them] Some at home say a family known for {KNOWNFOR} would end it quicker.
[us] We have our own walls to watch.
[us] Is that business with {THEN} over now?
[them] Over, and people at home have gone back to talking about other things.
[us] Such as?
[them] Your family, for one.
[us] Has {THEN} let up at home?
[them] Not yet, and some there talk of walking all the way here for your family's help.
[us] Tell them the gate is open to the sick.
[them] {THEN} has passed at home, I'm glad to say.
[us] That's a relief.
[them] Some said if it hadn't, they'd have come to your family, known for {KNOWNFOR} as it is.
[them] {NOW} leads us now, and asked me about {HOUSE} before I left.
[us] What did you tell them?
[them] The truth, mostly.
[them] Our town has a new head now, {NOW}.
[us] Does {NOW} know of us?
[them] Of {HOUSE}, at least, that name gets around.
[us] How did the harvest go, in the end?
[them] Well enough, though nobody at home sets a table like your family's.
[us] You'll have to come back and eat with us, then.
[us] Did that trade you mentioned come to anything?
[them] Some, but our traders say they'd rather deal with your family.
[us] Then send them our way.
[them] The war with {THEN} is over, you'll be glad to hear.
[us] I am, for all your sakes.
[them] Our young ones had hoped to fight beside a family known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Did {THEN} ever settle down?
[them] It did, and now people at home have time to gossip about families like yours.
[us] I'm not sure I like the sound of that.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on at home?
[them] Still, so it's good to sit a while with a family known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Sit as long as you like.
[us] How's that work of yours coming along?
[them] Slowly, and I keep hearing your family is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Come and see some of it, then.
[them] You asked after my family last time, so I'll ask after yours.
[us] We're well enough, all of {HOUSE}.
[them] Good, that's all anyone can ask.
[us] Is {THEN} still at the head of your town?
[them] Still, and even {THEN} knows of {HOUSE} by now.
[us] Is {THEN} still leading your people?
[them] Still, and {THEN} knows your family's name as well as anyone does.
[us] How is {THEN} doing?
[them] Holding on, and asking about your family's {KNOWNFOR} whenever I visit.
[them] My family hasn't forgotten what lies between us and your colony.
[us] Nor have we.
[them] Then we understand each other.
[them] There's a grudge between my house and your colony, and it isn't mine to drop.
[us] Whose is it, then?
[them] Whoever comes after me, maybe.
[them] Our elders keep the count of what your colony owes us, and they forget nothing.
[us] Then they could teach us something about remembering.
